span.p:
Visitor opens the
T Levels page

div.style: color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Show a grey, locked button:
'Log in to download PDF'

div.style: color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;

span.p:
They click it and are taken
to the sign-in page

div.style: color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;

span.p:
After signing in, they come
back to the same subject

div.style: color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;

span.p:
They click it. Our server checks again:
still signed in, and is it
one of our files?

div.style: color: rgb(15, 17, 17) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 340px; text-align: center;

span.p: The files are kept in a private folder, so this check is the only way to get them.
